newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher led by blue chips.

text.p: Stocks closed higher on Wednesday after falling interest rates and rising customer deposits at securities houses sent blue chips rallying in late trading, brokers said.

"Falling interest rates made investors believe that the impact from the collapse of two major companies this year had fizzled out," Chang Kun-woo of Daishin Securities said, referring to the failure of the Hanbo Group and Sammi Group.
The index ended 5.87 points higher at 678.86.
The releases of monthly vehicle sales figures by three major carmakers had no immediate impact, brokers said.
Customer deposits were estimated to have risen by about 40 billion won on Tuesday to three trillion won, brokers said.
Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds continued to fall to 12.48 percent on Tuesday from 12.5 percent on Monday after hitting a high of 13.00 percent last week.
Capital Intelligence's lowering of ratings on major local banks, reflecting Sammi Steel Co's collapse two weeks ago, added pressure on the already ailing bank sector.
Commercial Bank of Korea fell 120 won to 4,110, Hanil Bank 160 won to 4,790 and Shinhan Bank 100 won to 10,400.
Hyundai Motor, which announced a 7.6 percent drop in March vehicle sales, rose 900 won to 25,600. Kia Motors, whose vehicle sales rose 11.6 percent in March, closed flat at 16,000 won.
Recent sharp drops on Wall Street, hit by talks of a possible further interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve, had no impact on the market.
